text:
maria: quick heads-up — brought up zephyr-6b (distilled) across int4/int8/fp16 slices. int4/int8 give solid cost+latency wins but we're seeing a reproducible quality regression on long-form summarization (>1024 tokens). need recommendations for routing + unit-econ guidance for product.

josh: can you drop the quick econ numbers?

maria: sure — rough macros from yesterday's A/B bench (1M token baseline):
```
fp16: $120 / 1M tokens, avg latency 220ms/token
int8: 0.60x cost (~$72), latency ~170ms/token
int4-hybrid: 0.35x cost (~$42), latency ~150ms/token
```

li: interesting. where's the quality hit quantified?

maria: eval-bot posted snapshots: rougeL on long summarization dataset dropped from 46.3 (fp16) -> 42.1 (int8) -> 37.8 (int4). short Q/A and chat tasks look fine (within +-1.5 pts).

eval-bot: summary of last run: {"dataset":"long-summ-5k","fp16":46.3,"int8":42.1,"int4":37.8} — breaking patterns at >1k context due to hallucinated endings and truncated coherence.

arjun: any hypothesis? KV cache truncation or attention precision loss?

maria: we traced to two factors: (1) int4 token-level quant noise compounds over long prefix leading to weaker global coherence; (2) our prefix-KV caching behavior is slightly different between slices — int4 path omits a small corrective attenuation we use in fp16.

ben: can we do hybrid decoding: run key layers in int4 but last 4 decoder layers in fp16? how much overhead?

josh: microbench showed mixed-precision last-4-layers adds ~12% cost vs pure int4, still 0.4x vs fp16. latency up ~8ms/token.

maria: proposed operational plan for product routing (short form):
- route queries <=512 tokens -> int4-hybrid (default)
- 513–1024 tokens -> int8 (balance cost + quality)
- >1024 tokens or summarization task -> fp16 or int4-with-last4-fp16 fallback (depending on SLA)
- if eval confidence drops (delta rougeL > 2.5) trigger automatic canary rollback for that route and notify #eng-oncall

sara: for GTN we need a simple recommended default. product wants single knob they can use. can we provide a recommended "latency-tier" mapping?

maria: recommended two presets for product:
- "economy": use int4-hybrid for <=512, int8 for 513–1024, fp16 for >1024 (saves ~55% cost vs always-fp16)
- "safety": use int8 up to 2048, fp16 beyond (saves ~30% cost, minimal quality risk)
Note: both include automatic quality checks and 5% canary for new model pushes.

li: what's the suggested A/B plan to validate user-facing metrics?

maria: propose 4-week ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% per preset with concurrent offline evals and live signal tracking (CTR for summarization viewers, helpdesk escalations). rollback threshold: user-impact metric degrade >1.5 std dev or eval delta >3 points.

ben: logging + tracing: we should tag every response with model_slice and quant_profile so we can attribute regressions. also add sampling of full-token-latent dumps for flagged queries.

deploy-bot: canary config applied: zephyr-6b:int4-hybrid -> 1% traffic on dedicated test pool (infra-id: z6-int4-canary). :white_check_mark:

maria: follow-ups: (1) eng-ml to implement last-4-layer fp16 hybrid fastpath + perf guard (arjun + ben), (2) infra to add model_slice tagging (josh), (3) product to pick default preset (sara). aiming to finish pilot rollout by next Tue.

sara: will pick "economy" for PLG default but enable "safety" for enterprise tenants by config. will send short doc to GTN.

arjun: quick note on eval: I'll run adversarial long-context prompts (edge cases) and push failing examples to the model QA board.

maria: thanks all — adding a small playbook snippet in the doc repo later. ping me if you need the raw eval traces. :rocket:
